english_verification.review_scope: Read the actual formation decision, glassworks mission effect, and current English flavour text about glassmaking, the pioneer settlement, cobalt glass, and trade. Read the actual fixed-revision Wiki chunk for the ancient Hold. The Wiki passage supports the pre-1444 Hold history, not the formed I12 campaign or its current mechanics; no full mission audit was performed. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The Wiki describes the ancient Orlghelovar Hold and does not establish a modern I12 starting country or post-formation history. The source phrase 月神之泪 has no verified one-to-one English localization here; the article uses the verified native material terms azhalngiv/damestear and Black Damestear without asserting a literal equivalence.
Two suggested comparison-country names in the original source could not be verified as native English identities and are explicitly marked unverified in the overlay.

rationale.campaign_length: The 89 direct I12 mission definitions unfold in phases.
rationale.colonization: Forming from an Adventurer company and expanding through the mountains require opening new territory.
rationale.complexity: Trade goods, buildings, money, and technology thresholds stack together.
rationale.dark_story: Dangerous experiments and resource wars occur, but a dark narrative is not the dominant theme.
rationale.difficulty: Long construction chains can create delays and resource bottlenecks; this has not been tested in play.
rationale.diplomacy: Surface trade routes and relations with neighboring Dwarves affect development.
rationale.early_pressure: This depends on the Adventurer predecessor and the regional situation when the old Hold is reclaimed.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Mana Glass, dark crystal, and artifice weapons enter the later main story.
rationale.narrative_density: The ancient Hold's fall, revival of its craft, and growth into a research state form clear phases.
rationale.tall_play: The Hold, workshops, university, and industrial facilities are central.
rationale.trade_economy: Cobalt glass, surface markets, and high-value trade are core features.
rationale.warfare: War serves access to resources and trade routes.

identity.appearance: Formed after a qualified Dwarven Adventurer company reclaims the ancient Hold; the Hold's history does not make it a starting country in 1444.
identity.formation_scope: Control Hold 4238 and meet the Adventurer reform, technology, urban-development, and peace requirements to form I12 and receive its replacement mission tree.
predecessors: A qualifying Dwarven Adventurer company (no single Tag is uniquely required).

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Adopting new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: In the past, the dwarves of Orlghelovar were known as the "Glasslords". It is said they mastered the art of glassmaking and taught its secrets to humans who helped it eventually flourish in places like the Bulwar. As their name implies, the Cobalt dwarves were fond of using cobalt as a pigment, most famously in dark blue Orlghelovar glass - it is said that many ancient human glass relics can trace their origins to the renowned hold.

description.text: The Cobalt Dwarves were innovative pioneers within the Dwarovar. While some dwarves drew complacent with the power and reach of the empire, within Orlghelovar research of the unknown natural world was still ongoing. Many papers outlining discoveries in physics and other arcane subjects constantly drafted, outlining topics such as Halanna's breath or the applications of mystical plants harvested in the Deepwoods by their Flint neighbours.

description.text: It is said that Orlghelovar was one of the richest holds in the Dwarovar, and was so concerned with their greed and arrogance with trade with the rising kingdoms of Bulwar, it fell with ease to the orc and goblin hordes lack of due diligence repairs on their gates and providing meagre supplies to their army. Their greed and decadence serves as a warning to all dwarves up to this day.

description.text:
In order to keep ties to lucrative markets the lords of Orlghelovar fostered relations with their key market: the richest and most decadent holds of Aul-Dwarov. In 6735 BA the master glassmaker and head of the Glasshammer cartel, Okkid Glasshammer, set up a yearly convention in Amldihr showcasing the new goods and styles from the hold in Orlghelovar. This eventually became the foremost gathering of glassmakers and glass-buyers across the empire, with many a masterpiece ordered during the event.

For Orlghelovar, however, it also kept them in the loop with the coming-and-goings of the rest of the Dwarovar.

description.text: Daylight is a pleasure not many dwarves can experience except for some select surface holds, as it is found only beyond the hold's gates. Not so in Orlghelovar where the Cobalt Dwarves developed contraptions using mirrors and lenses to fill their hold with daylight and replace artificial light sources, providing a bright and unique environment. The daylight brought new life to the hold, with indoor flora growing where it couldn't before which became an experience that many dwarves desired for their own homes.

description.text: Glassblowing requires strong lungs, which can be used for other purposes as well. It is no surprise then that the Cobalt dwarves were famed wind instrumentalists, the sound of their trumpets and horns echoing deep underground. When they marched to war, they were led by dedicated marching bands which greatly inspired the troops and improved their organisation.

description.text: Guntîrhug, the renowned university of Orlghelovar, attracted many dwarves from all over the Dwarovar, as many of the greatest experts of their fields gathered and lectured there. While in other holds they specialised at staring into the sky or in inventing engineering contraptions, all fields of science for researching and documenting the natural world were holistically represented within Guntîrhug. Many students were infamously said to have superiority complexes from staying among the greatest intellectuals, known to repel many peers beyond Guntîrhug. Regardless, such a holistic and wide-ranging education did have many benefits to both students and to Orlghelovar.

player_overview.avoid_if: For players who dislike preparatory buildings, gathering materials, research waits, and long campaigns.
player_overview.how_it_plays: First form around the old Hold and restore the glass industry; then connect mining, trade, and the university; later invest in Mana Glass, medicine, and artifice weapons.
player_overview.overview: The Glasslords are a country formed after a Dwarven Adventurer company reclaims an ancient Hold. Begin by restarting the glassworks and cobalt production, connect the mountain economy to Bulwari trade, then let the university, medicine, Mana Glass, and artifice weapons carry the craft forward. This is a long industrial revival: profits and technology are enticing, but preparatory construction, rare materials, and research thresholds continually slow expansion.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy Dwarven Holds, industrial chains, trade, and research that advances in stages.
signature_features: The restoration of an ancient Cobalt Dwarven glass Hold connects underground industry with surface trade.
Glass, medicine, and university research gradually lead to magical materials and artifice weapons.
Research and supply-chain thresholds shape the campaign more than conquest alone.
player_overview.tagline: Rekindle the Cobalt Dwarves' blue-glass furnaces and turn a lost Hold into a scientific center.

reasons: The glass industry develops naturally into research and artifice.
The ancient Hold connects to Bulwari trade.
Medicine and the university make it more than a war-focused Dwarven country.
warnings: The mission tree has building, trade-good, and material thresholds.
The long research route can involve substantial waiting.

positive_indicators: The university and natural-science research are central national projects.
Doctors and medicine feature in the mission route.
Surface-dwelling human merchants can settle and participate in the market.
values.rationale: The university, medicine, and trade provide public benefits; open commerce and text allowing non-Dwarven settlement support relatively broad recognition. Armament and resource competition reduce restraint; wealth or technology alone does not add to a good-alignment score.
red_flags: Military action to obtain scarce resources carries an expansionist cost.
Some later research involves risky experiments.
